title: Tero's remark to Merlin Sheldrake on mushrooms at the start and end of forest life cycles

tellings.quote: Not just mushrooms, but other really sacred foods tend to live in these like the beginning of the forest lifecycle, or at the end of the forest lifecycle, where there's extremely nothing else growing almost, like pioneer, or at the end of it when there's massive biodiversity.

plain: Mushrooms and other 'really sacred foods' tend to grow either at the very start of a forest's life cycle, when almost nothing else grows, or at its end, when there is 'massive biodiversity'. That is the point Tero Isokauppila, a guest who talks about mushrooms, says he made around 2020 to the fungus researcher Merlin Sheldrake. He tells it as his own remark, part of his larger case that these foods hold a special place in nature.
